title: solve.status (v1): solve.started | solve.completed
description: DRAFT by osovyk for review; owner TBD. solver -> timetable, topic solve.status, key school_id (one topic, so the partition keeps started before completed). The envelope `type` selects the payload. timetable accepts solve.started only for a queued job and solve.completed from any non-final state.

started_at.description: timetable computes run_deadline_at = started_at + time limit + margin (>= 90 s).

status.description: OPTIMAL/FEASIBLE carry a timetable; INFEASIBLE carries conflicts; UNKNOWN = no solution within the limit; MODEL_INVALID = technical failure, never retried (error.code says why); EXPIRED = skipped because queue_deadline_at had passed. OPTIMAL is relative to the solver's model, which includes the per-row daily cap (quality rule, ADR 2026-11-04 §1): with stats.quality_relaxed=false it is optimal among timetables that respect the cap, not necessarily for the uncapped problem of spec §04; with quality_relaxed=true the cap was dropped and the model is the spec §04 problem.

lessons.description: Weekly template; ids only (no teacher signatures).

stats.description: Optional provenance and quality of a solve (shown in /load as build time; bench RQ1).

objective.description: W * primary + secondary of the best solution found.

best_bound.description: Proven upper bound of the objective of the solver's model; the gap is (best_bound - objective) / best_bound. With quality_relaxed=false the model includes the per-row daily cap, so this bounds capped timetables only and is not an upper bound for the uncapped spec §04 problem; with quality_relaxed=true it is.

input_sha256.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON of the validated request data.

quality_relaxed.description: true = the per-day row cap was dropped to find a solution (ADR quality ladder).
